amendments.rule: A construct noun cannot take the article, so a pointed `בַּ` before one is preposition-only and the English *the* is supplied. Follow MACULA's morphology rather than the pointing. Where the chain's *nomen rectum* does carry an article, that morpheme takes the *the* the ASV writes for the chain even though English fronts it to the phrase's left edge and renders the rectum anarthrously — `לֻחֹת הָאֲבָנִים` → *the two tables of stone*, `כּוּר הַבַּרְזֶל` → *the furnace of iron*. Supply a *the* on a construct noun only where no article morpheme is present, or for a second English *the* in a multi-level chain, which the article's own leaves for the outer construct: `לְבַב כָּל בְּנֵי הָאָדָם` → *the hearts of all the children of men*. **Fronting is what the anarthrous rendering forces, not a preference for the phrase's left edge.** Where the ASV instead renders the rectum arthrously, writing a *the* before the construct and another before the rectum — `מִשְׁפַּחַת הַקְּהָתִי` → *the families of the Kohathites*, `בְּנֵי הַקְּהָתִי` → *the sons of the Kohathites*, `שְׂדֵה הָעִיר` → *the fields of the city*, `מִשְׁפְּחוֹת הַלֵּוִי` → *the families of the Levites* — nothing is fronted: the article takes the *the* standing before its own word and the construct takes a supplied one, exactly as an outer construct does in a multi-level chain. Count the ASV's *the*s and read which word each stands before, as rule 47 reads which word its single *the* stands before. **A construct relation the ASV recasts as an English possessive is not a fronting either.** Where the ASV writes the rectum as a possessive standing before its head noun — `מִלַּת מַלְכָּא` → *the king's matter*, `שַׁלִּיטָא דִּי מַלְכָּא` → *the king's captain*, `שַׁעַר הַמֶּלֶךְ` → *the king's gate* — the *the* at the phrase's left edge stands before the possessor's own word, because an English possessive expression takes the determiner of the possessor and not of the head noun. So the article on the rectum takes it and the construct noun keeps only its own word, a present article morpheme taking its English before a supplied one does; supply a *the* on the construct only where the ASV writes a second one, as `רַב טַבָּחַיָּא דִּי מַלְכָּא` → *the captain of the king's guard* does. Do not read the left edge as evidence of fronting: what fronting answers to is an anarthrous rectum, and here the rectum is the very word the *the* determines. **Read that as the determiner of the possessive, not as the word *the*, and read it whether or not the possessor carries an article of its own.** An English possessive expression takes the determiner of the possessor whatever that determiner is, so an indefinite *a* standing at the phrase's left edge stands before the possessor's word exactly as a *the* does, and where the possessor's word carries no article morpheme the determiner the ASV supplies still goes to that word rather than to the construct noun: `נְשִׂיא בֵית־אָב` → *a prince of* ***a fathers*** *house* gives *a fathers* to `אָב` and *of ... house* to `בַּיִת`, discontinuous around the possessive under rule 25. This is rule 15's supplied determiner placed by this rule's own reasoning — the noun that licenses an English *a* in such a phrase is the possessor, since *a father's house* is the house of *a* father — and the construct noun takes a determiner of its own only where the ASV writes a second one, on the terms just given. A `דִּי` or other relational morpheme standing between the two nouns is rendered inside the possessive and shares the rectum's unit under rule 30. **A rectum that is a proper name is not an exception.** An article MACULA segments off a toponym takes the ASV's *the* on the same terms as one on a common noun, and is never set aside as lexicalized in the name: `בְּנֵי הָרָמָה` → *The children of Ramah* and `אַנְשֵׁי בֵית אֵל וְהָעָי` → *The men of Beth el and Ai* give the single written *the* to the article and leave the construct noun bare. **But an article the ASV spells into its name is already rendered.** Where the rectum is transliterated with its article — `בְּנֵי הַסֹּפֶרֶת` → *the children of Hassophereth* — the article shares the name's unit under rule 30, it has taken its *the* inside that English word rather than as a separate one, and the *the* the ASV does write stands before the construct as a supplied one. Read the transliteration before counting: nothing is fronted from an article English has already spelled out. Mark the article `unrepresented` only where the ASV writes no *the* for the phrase at all, as in `הֶעָרִים הָאֵלֶּה` → *these cities*.
amendments.why: NUM.25.14 and NUM.25.15 both render `נְשִׂיא בֵית־אָב` as *a prince of a fathers house*, and the chapter put the *a* on `אָב`. Rule 29 already gives the reason — an English possessive expression takes the determiner of the possessor and not of the head noun — but every example it cites is a written *the* on a rectum that carries an article morpheme, so as it stood it said nothing about an indefinite determiner or about a possessor with no article of its own, and rule 15's *belongs to the noun that licenses it* pulls a reader toward the head noun *house*. The added sentences state which noun licenses it, in this rule's own terms, and change nothing about the arthrous cases the rule already settles. Returned as an amendment rather than a new rule so the over-broad reading is corrected where it stands; the construction (`בֵּית אָב`, `נְשִׂיא בֵית אָב`) recurs throughout Numbers and Chronicles, and nothing in the corpus supplied for this chapter bears against it.

conventions: המדינית is aligned three ways in this chapter and all three are licensed, so do not level them. NUM.25.6 renders the phrase indefinitely (a Midianitish woman), so the article is unrepresented and the supplied a and woman join the adjective's unit; NUM.25.14 writes the Midianitish woman, so the article takes the the and the supplied woman still joins the adjective; NUM.25.15 writes אשה in the Hebrew and a single the for the whole phrase, so the noun's article takes that the, the gentilic's agreement article is unrepresented under rule 47, and the adjective keeps only Midianitish because the noun it would have been expanded with is written.

בעל פעור is one MACULA lemma spanning two source tokens, and this chapter splits it into two units, one per token, in NUM.25.3 and NUM.25.5, because the ASV writes two English words (Baal peor). Rule 30's one-English-word condition is what decides it; a single lemma across two tokens is not itself a reason to fuse.

Rule 30 fusions in this chapter are recorded with status aligned rather than noncompositional: מעל to from (NUM.25.8, NUM.25.11), בתוך to among (NUM.25.11), תחת אשר to because (NUM.25.13), לכן to Wherefore (NUM.25.12). The corpus records both statuses for such fusions, so this is a chapter-wide choice and not a rule; noncompositional was reserved, per rule 6, for phrases that are genuinely indivisible rather than merely fused.

report: Read all 18 verses end to end against the candidate table, the validation report and the corpus precedent. No construction is analysed two ways with nothing in the source to license the difference, so patches is empty.

The three treatments of המדינית are each read off what the ASV writes: v6 renders the phrase indefinitely and the article is unrepresented under rule 29's closing sentence; v14 writes a the and the article takes it; v15 writes one the for a phrase carrying three articles, so the noun's article takes it and the gentilic's agreement article is unrepresented under rule 47. The supplied woman joins the adjective in vv. 6 and 14, where the Hebrew writes no noun, and not in v15, where אשה is written. Recorded as a convention so a later reader does not level them.

v11's two object markers differ because the ASV does: את־חמתי is written bare and unrepresented, while את־קנאתי takes the with through which the English verb reaches its object, which is rule 16's first family. v7's protasis waw takes the And when pair under rule 55 while the apodosis waw is unrepresented under rule 14, and the supplied it after ויַּרְא is the chapter's one added unit, which is what rule 44 requires of a pronoun supplied for a verb whose Hebrew writes no object.

The four rule-30 fusions (מעל to from twice, בתוך to among, תחת אשר to because, לכן to Wherefore) are uniform in status and head: all aligned rather than noncompositional, and all headed on the governing first morpheme except בתוך, which rule 23 names explicitly as heading on the construct noun. מתוך in v7 is split instead because the ASV spends a word on each morpheme, which is rule 30's condition and not an inconsistency with v11.

BSB: all nine disagreements are documented convention differences, not errors — rule 40 recastings with bare English objects (v2 לָ, v18 לכם twice), rule 27 (לאמר twice), rule 16 (object markers, vv. 4 and 17), the two Midianite articles above, and the bare apodosis waw of v7. Nothing was changed to improve the rate.

One amendment, to rule 29, on where the determiner of an English possessive recasting goes when it is indefinite and the possessor carries no article morpheme: בית־אב to a fathers house in vv. 14 and 15 puts the a on אב. No new rules — rule 44's phrasal particles across a discontinuity, rule 41 against rule 47 on a triple-article phrase, and rule 19's suffix-as-rectum in שניהם to both of them are all already stated and would only be restated.
